transcript:
Header: 2027-07-29 10:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Ethan Brooks (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SRE), Lina Ho (Redwood CSM); Grace Kim (AquinaBank Head of Platform), Arun Singh (Aquina ML), Maya Thompson (CTO), Leo Park (Infra), Sam O'Neill (Eng Manager)

AutoSummary (auto): Weekly POC sync for latency tuning. Reviewed last week's TTFT regressions on 8k seq streaming, kernel selection experiments, and infra traces. Agreed to run targeted kernel benchmarks and share logs; discuss dedicated pilot pricing and compliance gating.

Topics: TTFT / time-to-first-token, streaming first-chunk perf, sequence length distribution (4k vs 8k), kernel choices (triton fused kernels vs liquid-fuse), batching and KV cache, cold start vs warm latency, quantization impacts on perf, Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, compliance/SOC2 + KMS questions.

Transcript Body:
00:00 Ethan: All right, good morning everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call, then we'll go into the perf notes.
00:12 Grace: Morning. Grace here.
00:16 Maya: Maya, here.
00:18 Arun: Arun here.
00:21 Priya: Priya, I'm on.
00:25 Ethan: Cool. So main agenda - we saw the TTFT gap on 8k streaming where first token is 180-220ms vs our 90-110ms target on hosted. We want to walk through traces, kernel runs, and next steps.
00:40 Carlos: I'll share the perf sheet in chat, but TL;DR: cold-start TTFT is hurting when the model sharded across GPUs; warm-state with KV cache is fine, it's the very first chunk and the attention kernel selection.
00:58 Arun: Right, and to confirm our traffic pattern, ~70% of requests are 512-1k, 20% 2k-4k, and ~10% 6k-8k. So tail behavior matters a lot. We also stream incremental chunks with chunk size ~256 tokens.
01:20 Priya: That distribution explains why we see average latencies okay but tail TTFT spikes on 8k. Two immediate knobs: streaming chunk size and which kernel/compilation we use for long-seq attention.
01:34 Leo: On infra we see CPU overhead at the start of streams - some pre-processing sits on CPU while GPU kernels are initialized, maybe some hidden memcpy or cuBLAS init.
02:00 Ethan: Priya, can you summarize the kernel experiments you ran last night?
02:05 Priya: Yeah. I ran three variants: 1) default compiled Triton attention, 2) fused attention kernels optimized for long sequences (our team calls it \"liquid-fuse\" internally), and 3) fallback cuBLAS path with larger workspace. On short sequences (<1k) Triton was fine, but on 4k-8k the fused kernels gave 20-30% faster first-token times under warm runs. Cold TTFT improvement was smaller because of init costs. Also quantized int8 (nf4) reduced GPU memory and improved throughput but added ~10ms to TTFT for dequant steps.
02:48 Grace: Does NF4 mean we're trading off accuracy? We run some compliance evals so need to know quality delta.
02:54 Priya: We did a quick eval on our prompt set - quality delta within noise for generation tasks, for sensitive financial wording we saw a slight drop on rare templates. We'll include more evals if Aquina wants to push quant.
03:15 Maya: Important: for production we can't accept any noticeable regression on compliance phrasing detection. If quant gives small drop, maybe use it only on non-sensitive routes.
03:30 Ethan: Good call. Back to TTFT: Carlos mentioned CPU-to-GPU init. Carlos, any instrumentation that points to a fix?
03:40 Carlos: Yeah, the trace shows host-side serialization of request metadata and a synchronous memcpy before kernel launch. We can async that, and also pre-warm certain kernels to avoid the PTX JIT on first use. Also there is room to tweak our serving runtime to pre-allocate KV cache for anticipated seq length.
04:05 Arun: Pre-warming sounds useful but expensive. Does Redwood support pre-provisioned warm pools on Dedicated?
04:12 Priya: Yes, Dedicated has warm pools and pinning options. We can reserve warm capacity for peak windows. For Hosted, we do proactive warm-up heuristics but it's probabilistic.
04:28 Ethan: Ok, let's talk streaming chunk size. We tested 128 vs 256 vs 512 token chunks. What were the numbers?
04:36 Priya: 128 gave more RTPS overhead but smaller per-chunk compute; TTFT improved slightly vs 512 but increased total per-response overhead because more chunks = more RPCs. 256 seems a good middle ground; on fused kernels 256 yielded best tradeoff for 4k-8k.
05:05 Grace: Is there a way to do adaptive chunking based on predicted response length? We could pick 256 for long flows and 512 for short.
05:12 Priya: Yes, we can implement heuristics in the client: Redwood SDK supports chunk hints and adaptive streaming window. We can push a config in the next SDK build.
05:24 Maya: On kernel choice - what's the difference between Triton and your fused kernels? Is fused maintained upstream?
05:31 Priya: Triton is the general-purpose compiler; our fused kernels combine attention + rotary + dropout into a single CUDA kernel minimizing global memory traffic and multiple launches. It's maintained by our infra team and we run strict tests. We can expose kernel toggle per model variant.
05:52 Leo: Any compatibility issues with quant and fused kernels?
05:55 Priya: We support nf4 and 4-bit fused kernels; there are caveats for certain ops, but we've validated on the models you provided. Some corner cases require fallback to slower paths.
06:12 Ethan: Security / compliance question - Grace raised SOC2 / KMS earlier, anything blocking todays perf testing?
06:19 Grace: We need to ensure logs don't contain PII and that KMS endpoints are usable in our VPC. Also audit logs for key rotations.
06:29 Lina: On Redwood Private/Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS and provide audit logs; we'll send the SOC2 package and KMS integration doc after the call.
06:40 Grace: Great. Please also include the endpoints for HSM support.
06:44 Lina: Will do.
07:00 Ethan: Back to measurements - Priya, can you indicate what you'll run for the kernel benchmark?
07:04 Priya: I'll run a 4x matrix: sequence lengths [512, 2048, 4096, 8192], kernels [Triton, fused, cuBLAS-fallback], quant modes [FP16, nf4]. For each we capture cold TTFT, warm TTFT, median and p95 end-to-end latency with streaming chunking at 128/256/512. I'll also capture GPU occupancy and memcpy times.
07:30 Arun: Please capture the first-chunk time separately from chunk-to-chunk times. We found first-chunk is dominated by host-side preproc.
07:38 Priya: Yep will do.
07:40 Carlos: We'll add tracing to show synchronous memcpy durations and kernel launch delays as separate fields.
07:47 Ethan: Sounds good. Next, Dedicated pilot - Grace, are you leaning Dedicated to fix warm-pools and pinning?
07:55 Grace: We're open but need to see cost delta. If Dedicated reduces tail TTFT by 30% and gives predictability, that might be worth the commit. We need a clear SLO and rollback plan.
08:10 Ethan: I'll send pricing scenarios: small reserved pool vs auto-scale with burst. We'll include SLO examples and can do a short pilot month.
08:20 Maya: Also include fallback policies - e.g., if Dedicated is saturated, route to hosted smaller model variant. We need a clear graceful degradation plan.
08:30 Ethan: Yep that's standard.
08:35 Priya: One more thing - we noticed that sequence packing for batch runs helps throughput but hurts TTFT for single requests; for Aquina's traffic mix packing is important during peak batch windows but we should keep low-latency lanes for interactive queries. We can expose packing thresholds per route.
08:55 Grace: Good idea. We'll want default low-latency lane for user-facing endpoints.
09:02 Sam: Quick Q: can you show a sample of the benchmark result formats so we can ingest into our observability?
09:08 Priya: I'll push CSV + small JSON summary into the shared folder and include a sample Grafana dashboard.
09:14 Carlos: Also FYI for instrumentation, attach request IDs so we can trace from client logs to kernel traces.
09:20 Priya: We'll add request_id header support in the next minor SDK.
09:25 Ethan: Quick recap - Priya runs kernel benchmarks and posts results (due 2027-08-02), Carlos uploads traces (due 2027-07-31), Ethan shares Dedicated pricing and pilot doc (due 2027-08-04), Redwood to send SOC2/KMS docs (Lina) and schedule deep-dive if needed.
09:48 Grace: Sounds good. Anything else?
09:52 Maya: Not from me.
09:54 Ethan: All right thanks everyone. We'll follow up in the thread with the shared links.
10:00 Meeting end.

Attachments/links referenced: perf_sheet_q3_drive_link.xlsx (in chat), dedicated_pricing_draft.pdf (to be shared), soc2_kms_integration.md (to be shared), sample_grafana_dashboard.json (to be shared).

Notes on transcription imperfections: speaker labels may be slightly off at times; 'liquid-fuse' name is internal shorthand; 'KV cash' typo appears in early auto captions then corrected in conversation.
